Their design separates rotor and stator assemblies, enabling specialized supply chains.

Gearbox.reasoning: Primary raw material for gearbox gears and casing due to its mechanical strength and durability; universally essential and standard in gearbox manufacturing.

Gearbox.name: Chromium
Gearbox.reasoning: Used for plating or alloying to enhance wear resistance and corrosion protection of gearbox components; standard practice with few substitutes for corrosion resistance.

Gearbox.name: Nickel
Gearbox.reasoning: Alloyed with steel for improving toughness and corrosion resistance in gear and shaft materials; commonly used though alternative alloys exist.

Gearbox.name: Copper
Gearbox.reasoning: Sometimes used in bushings or electrical grounding in gearbox assemblies; not always present but common due to good conductivity and lubrication compatibility.

Gearbox.name: Aluminum
Gearbox.reasoning: Used selectively for lightweight gearbox housings or covers; alternatives exist but aluminum is a preferred low-weight material.
